documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
21 y/o F here to establish. Previously seen at a pediatric practice in town through high school and college health since; aged out and her parents wanted her somewhere she could reach by text. No complaints today.

PMH: none. No hospitalizations. PSH: none.
Meds: none. No OTC or supplements.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father with HTN. Mother with hypothyroidism. Maternal grandmother had breast cancer at 65. No early heart disease, no colon cancer known.
SH: full-time at the university, works part time in retail on weekends. Lives in an apartment off campus with a roommate. Never smoked, never vaped. Alcohol a couple of drinks a month, social. No drugs. Sexually active; declines to go into more detail today, agreeable to routine STI screening.
Gyn: menarche around 12, cycles regular. Has not had a Pap yet.

ROS: negative in full.

Exam: well, pleasant. HEENT clear, TMs normal. Neck supple, thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, NT, no masses. Skin clear. Neuro grossly normal. Mood bright.
PHQ-2 0, GAD-7 2, AUDIT-C 2.

A/P: healthy young adult, establishing care.
- Baseline lipids, CBC, CMP.
- One-time HIV and hepatitis C screens; urine GC/CT given age.
- Immunizations: will pull the pediatric record. Flu shot next month when clinic stock arrives.
- First Pap due; she would rather do it next visit. Fine, we will plan for next fall.
- Gave her the practice cell number. Return in a year.

Adolescent: Tdap 06/2012; MenACWY 06/2012 and booster 08/2017; HPV 9-valent 06/2015 and 12/2015 (2-dose series, started before 15).
COVID-19 Pfizer primary series 04/2021 and 05/2021, per state registry.

Abstracted to the immunization list. — front desk

documents.title: Gynecology Office Note
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY PRACTICE — CLINIC NOTE
Date of service: 12/30/2024
Patient: Samantha Kimball, DOB 04/29/2001
Copy to: primary care physician

Reason for visit: 5 days of burning with urination, urinary frequency and yellow vaginal discharge.

HPI: 23-year-old seen same day. Symptoms began about 5 days ago. LMP roughly three weeks ago; no change in her cycles. Reports multiple sexual partners over the last six months with inconsistent condom use.

Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: maternal grandmother with breast cancer at 65; father with hypertension; mother with hypothyroidism.
Social: never smoker; alcohol 2-3 drinks per month; university student, works part time in retail.

Exam: T 37.8 C (100.0 F). Well-appearing. Abdomen soft. Speculum: purulent discharge from the cervical os. Bimanual: cervical motion tenderness.

Testing: urine pregnancy test negative today. Urine GC/CT NAAT, HIV-1/2 Ag/Ab, RPR and HBsAg sent.
Results (addended 1/1/2025): N. gonorrhoeae DETECTED; C. trachomatis not detected. HIV Ag/Ab negative. RPR nonreactive. HBsAg negative.

Assessment: gonococcal cervicitis.

Plan: ceftriaxone 500 mg IM given in clinic today. Advised no intercourse for 7 days after treatment and until partners from the last 60 days are tested and treated; she will notify partners. Condoms counseled. Retest in 3 months. Patient informed of the positive result by phone 1/2.

Electronically signed, attending gynecologist

documents.title: Gynecology Office Note
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY PRACTICE — FOLLOW-UP NOTE
Date of service: 03/31/2025
Patient: Samantha Kimball, DOB 04/29/2001
cc: PCP

CC: painful urination and frequency x5 days.

HPI: Known to us from 12/30/2024, when she had gonococcal cervicitis treated with ceftriaxone. Now about three months out, with five days of dysuria and urinary frequency. About two weeks ago she had unprotected intercourse with a new partner. No vaginal discharge, no bleeding.

Meds: none currently. Allergies: NKDA.
Social: never smoker. Alcohol occasional, 2-3 drinks/month. Student; part-time retail.
Family hx: as previously documented (maternal grandmother breast cancer at 65, father HTN, mother hypothyroidism).

Exam: vital signs within normal limits. Abdomen soft, no tenderness. Pelvic: cervical motion tenderness present.

UA (in office): leukocyte esterase positive, nitrite negative; microscopy WBC 10-20/hpf, RBC 0-2/hpf, no bacteria and no yeast seen.
GC/CT NAAT sent — resulted 4/2: N. gonorrhoeae not detected, C. trachomatis not detected.

Impression: pyuria without bacteriuria plus cervical motion tenderness in a patient with recent gonorrhea — treating as suspected pelvic inflammatory disease.

Plan:
- Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM x1 given today.
- Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID x14 days.
- Metronidazole 500 mg PO BID x14 days; avoid alcohol.
- Abstain until the course is done and the new partner is treated. Condoms.
- Return or go to the ED for fever, worsening pelvic pain or vomiting, or if no better in 72 hours.

Signed, attending gynecologist

documents.title: Phone Check-in
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called her after the gyn letter from 3/31 came in. Day 5 of doxy and metronidazole; some nausea with the metronidazole if she takes it on an empty stomach, better with food. Burning already easing. No fever, no worsening pain.
NAAT from 3/31 negative for both GC and CT, so the December gonorrhea is treated — taking cervicitis off the active list. Suspected PID stays on until she finishes and feels well.
Med list updated with the 14-day courses. Finish every dose; no alcohol with metronidazole. Text me if she gets fever or worse pain.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT — PHYSICIAN RECORD
Arrival 01/01/2026 11:05. Patient: Samantha Kimball, 24 F.

Chief complaint: fever, lower belly pain, discharge x2 days.

HPI: 24 y/o F with gonococcal cervicitis in 12/2024 (ceftriaxone) and suspected PID in 3/2025 treated as an outpatient, who presents with two days of fever, diffuse lower abdominal pain and vaginal discharge. LMP about 3 weeks ago. States there is no chance she is pregnant. Multiple partners, condoms inconsistently.

PMH: as above. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
SH: never smoker, occasional alcohol.

Triage: T 39.2 C (102.5 F), HR 110, BP 100/60, RR 18, SpO2 98% RA.

Exam: uncomfortable, nontoxic. Mucous membranes moist. Heart tachycardic, regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, diffusely tender across the lower abdomen, no rebound, no RUQ tenderness. Pelvic (chaperoned): mucopurulent discharge at the os; cervical motion tenderness; bilateral adnexal tenderness, no mass.

Labs: WBC 15.0 K/uL with 80% neutrophils. Hgb 12.5. Platelets and BMP unremarkable. Urine hCG negative. GC/CT NAAT sent, pending at disposition.
Imaging: pelvic US (TA/TV) — normal uterus and ovaries, no TOA, no free fluid.

ED course: acetaminophen for fever. Ceftriaxone 1 g IV, doxycycline 100 mg and metronidazole 500 mg started. Repeat T 38.4, HR 96 at 15:40.

Impression: acute pelvic inflammatory disease, febrile and tachycardic; no abscess on ultrasound.
Disposition: admitted to gynecology for IV antibiotics.

Electronically signed, ED attending

Take 2 tablets by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain or fever
Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily to complete 14 days total (through 1/14); no alcohol

documents.title: Discharge Summary — Gynecology
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 01/01/2026 from the ED; discharged 01/03/2026. Service: gynecology.
Patient: Samantha Kimball, DOB 04/29/2001. Allergies: NKDA.

Principal diagnosis: acute pelvic inflammatory disease.
History: gonococcal cervicitis 12/2024, treated with ceftriaxone; suspected PID 3/2025, outpatient treatment.

Presentation: 2 days of fever, lower abdominal pain and discharge; febrile to 39.2 C with HR 110 and BP 100/60 in the ED. CMT, bilateral adnexal tenderness, mucopurulent cervical discharge. WBC 15.0, 80% neutrophils, Hgb 12.5. Urine hCG negative. Pelvic US without tubo-ovarian abscess.

Hospital course: admitted for parenteral therapy given fever and tachycardia. Ceftriaxone 1 g IV q24h, doxycycline 100 mg q12h and metronidazole 500 mg q12h. Fever broke overnight; afebrile from the morning of 1/2 with HR in the 70s-80s. CBC 1/2: WBC 9.2. Abdominal tenderness lessened steadily; tolerating diet. GC/CT NAAT from the ED returned 1/2 — both not detected.

Condition at discharge: stable, afebrile, ambulating, pain controlled with acetaminophen.

Discharge medications:
- Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID through 1/14 (14 days total)
- Metronidazole 500 mg PO BID through 1/14 (14 days total); no alcohol
- Acetaminophen as needed

Instructions: no intercourse until the course is finished and partners are evaluated and treated. Return for fever, worsening pain or vomiting. Follow up with PCP within one week; repeat GC/CT in about 3 months.

Dictated by gynecology attending

documents.title: was in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I went to the ER on New Year's with a high fever and pelvic pain and they kept me two nights for IV antibiotics — they said PID again. Home now and feeling a lot better, on doxycycline and metronidazole for another 11 days. They said to see you this week.

documents.title: RE: was in the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry you went through that — glad you're home and improving. I'll ask the hospital for the records Monday. Front desk will text you a time Wednesday. If the fever comes back or the pain worsens before then, text me or go back in.

documents.title: Records Request — Hospital
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Called hospital health information management for ED record, imaging and discharge summary from 1/1-1/3 admission. Release on file from the patient's portal consent. Faxed over at 10:15; indexed and routed to PCP.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 4 days after discharge. ED record, pelvic US and discharge summary from 1/1-1/3 reviewed before the visit.

S: Admitted 1/1-1/3 for PID (T 39.2, HR 110 on arrival, WBC 15.0, no TOA on US), IV ceftriaxone/doxy/metronidazole, home on oral doxy + metronidazole through 1/14. GC/CT from the ED negative. No fever since 1/2. Lower abdominal ache now mild and fading, acetaminophen once or twice a day. Taking both pills with food, no vomiting. Discharge lighter.

Meds: doxycycline 100 BID, metronidazole 500 BID (both through 1/14). NKDA.

O: afebrile, comfortable. Heart regular, normal rate. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, minimal lower tenderness to deep palpation, no guarding or rebound.

A/P: PID, third pelvic infection in about a year, improving on oral therapy.
- Finish both antibiotics; no alcohol with metronidazole.
- No sex until done and partners treated; condoms going forward.
- CBC today to confirm the white count is back down.
- Repeat GC/CT in early April — nurse visit, urine.
- Return precautions reviewed. Message me when she finishes.
